facts.program: PSE electric resistance to heat pump rebate
facts.claim: $1,500 rebate for replacing electric resistance heat with a qualifying air-source heat pump; $2,400 Efficiency Boost for income-qualified customers
facts.eligibility: Existing single-family PSE electric customer; primary heat must be electric resistance (forced-air furnace, baseboard, wall, radiant); no existing heat pump in main living area; PSE REP or Trade Ally contractor required; one rebate per home. Ductless: AHRI variable-speed, inverter, at least 3/4 ton, head in main living area, no ducting.
facts.notes: Page also says income-qualified customers upgrading from natural gas can get up to $4,000 (see wa-1).

facts.program: PSE moderate-income fuel-switching heat pump rebate
facts.claim: $4,000 rebate for income-qualified PSE natural gas customers who replace gas heat with a qualifying heat pump
facts.eligibility: Current PSE single-family natural gas customer; primary heat is PSE natural gas furnace, boiler or wall heater; income check on PSE's form; AHRI-certified ducted or ductless heat pump; PSE Trade Ally or REP; apply within 30 days of install; existing electric resistance or hybrid systems not eligible.

facts.program: PSE hybrid heat pump rebate (gas furnace plus heat pump)
facts.claim: $1,500 rebate ($2,400 Efficiency Boost) for adding a ducted heat pump to a natural gas furnace
facts.eligibility: PSE natural gas or dual-fuel customer; primary heat is a PSE natural gas furnace; ducted AHRI-certified air-source heat pump; balance point 30F or lower; PSE REP or Trade Ally; no existing heat pump.

facts.program: PSE heat pump to heat pump upgrade rebate
facts.claim: $1,500 rebate ($2,400 Efficiency Boost) for replacing an out-of-warranty ducted electric heat pump with a new one
facts.eligibility: Current primary heat is a centrally ducted all-electric air-source heat pump outside its manufacturer warranty, on PSE electricity; new system ducted and AHRI-certified; ductless not eligible; PSE REP or Trade Ally.

facts.program: PSE heat pump water heater rebate
facts.claim: $1,000 for a qualifying Tier 3 or Tier 4 heat pump water heater; $1,100 Efficiency Boost
facts.eligibility: Existing single-family PSE customer, unit must use PSE electricity after install; installed on or after Jan 1, 2026; apply within 30 days of installation; online PSE account.
facts.dates: Installed on or after 2026-01-01; no end date shown

facts.program: PSE weatherization (insulation and air sealing) instant rebates
facts.claim: Attic insulation $1.75 per sq ft up to $3,500 (R11 or less to R49) or $0.50 per sq ft up to $1,000 (R12-R19 to R49); wall and floor insulation $2.50 per sq ft up to $5,000 each; attic or floor air sealing $0.20 per sq ft up to $400 each; duct sealing and insulation up to $1,000; duct sealing only up to $550; advanced duct sealing up to $1,250
facts.eligibility: PSE electric or natural gas customer using PSE as primary space heat; single-family (four units or fewer) or manufactured home; PSE REP or Trade Ally takes the instant rebate off the invoice; attic amount depends on home type and existing insulation.
facts.notes: Income-qualified customers may get PSE's no-cost Home Weatherization Assistance Program (page does not give amounts).

facts.program: PSE energy-efficient window rebate
facts.claim: $50 or $100 per window by U-factor (up to $750 or $1,500); $200 per window (up to $2,000) Efficiency Boost or manufactured home
facts.eligibility: PSE electricity or natural gas is the primary heat; U-factor proof for each window or patio door; installed in conditioned space; apply within 60 days of installation.
facts.notes: The page text did not show the U-factor cut-offs for windows; they are not stated on HomePowerRebate pages.

facts.program: PSE smart thermostat rebate
facts.claim: $75 rebate for a qualifying smart thermostat; $175 Efficiency Boost (centrally heated homes); $130 Efficiency Boost for line-voltage thermostats
facts.eligibility: PSE residential customer with electric or PSE natural gas primary heat; one-thermostat central system (heat pump, furnace or boiler); no PSE thermostat rebate at the address in the last five years; apply within 60 days.

facts.program: PSE EV home charger rebate
facts.claim: Up to $300 for a qualifying Level 2 smart charger; income-qualified up to $600 plus up to $2,000 toward installation
facts.eligibility: PSE residential electric customer who owns, leases or has ordered an EV or plug-in hybrid; ENERGY STAR Level 2 smart charger prequalified by PSE; installed after 2024-01-01; apply within 60 days.

facts.program: PSE clothes washer and dryer rebates
facts.claim: The page headline lists washers $125, dryers $100 and heat pump dryers $400, but the rebate boxes below it show $75, $50 and $350 (higher with Efficiency Boost). The two sets do not match.
facts.eligibility: PSE electric customer; ENERGY STAR front-load washer, dryer or heat pump dryer from PSE's lists; apply within 60 days.
facts.notes: Amounts conflict inside the page; do not quote an amount.

facts.program: PSE Flex Batteries
facts.claim: Up to $1,000 per battery when you enroll, plus up to $500 per year for joining Flex events
facts.eligibility: Compatible home battery on PSE's grid; enrollment incentive depends on battery size; run by Uplight for PSE.

facts.program: PSE Efficiency Boost (income-qualified higher rebates)
facts.claim: About half of PSE customers qualify for higher rebates; check household size, monthly gross income and county on PSE's form
facts.eligibility: Income table is a PSE PDF dated June 2025; income limits not copied to HomePowerRebate pages

facts.program: Seattle City Light heat pump contractor instant discount
facts.claim: Contractor instant discount of $300 (HSPF2 8.1+), $400 (HSPF2 8.5+) or $600 (HSPF2 9.5+) on a qualifying heat pump, passed to you in the bid
facts.eligibility: Seattle City Light residential customers; available only through participating distributors and contractors; DIY installs not eligible.

facts.program: Seattle Clean Heat oil-to-electric rebate
facts.claim: $2,000 instant rebate for Seattle households heating with oil who convert to a qualified heat pump using a participating contractor; income-eligible households can get a no-cost conversion from the Seattle Office of Housing
facts.eligibility: Seattle household heating with oil; participating contractor.

facts.program: Seattle City Light heat pump water heater rebate
facts.claim: $750 per home through a contractor, a Home Depot or Lowe's instant coupon, or a post-purchase online rebate for a DIY install
facts.eligibility: Seattle City Light residential customer; ENERGY STAR Tier 3 or Tier 4 on the qualified list; the instant coupon cannot be stacked with the online rebate.

facts.program: Seattle City Light smart thermostat instant rebate
facts.claim: $50 per unit instant rebate on Mysa or Sinope smart thermostats bought online from the retailer
facts.eligibility: Seattle City Light residential customers only; buy through the retailer's City Light page.

facts.program: Seattle City Light net metering
facts.claim: Solar systems up to 100 kW AC get bill credits at the retail rate for power sent to the grid; extra credits roll forward; one extra meter on the same parcel can share credits
facts.amount: No rebate; bill credits at retail rate
facts.eligibility: Seattle City Light customer with an interconnection agreement
facts.notes: The page states no Seattle City Light solar rebate.

facts.program: Avista Washington heat pump contractor discount
facts.claim: Pass-through discount per outdoor system for air-source heat pumps under 5.4 tons: $300 (HSPF2 8.1, SEER2 15.2), $400 (HSPF2 8.5), $600 (HSPF2 9.5, SEER2 16.0); mini-splits for residential retrofit use the same three amounts; manufactured home heat pump up to 2.5 tons $400
facts.eligibility: Equipment must run on Avista electric or natural gas service; discount goes to the contractor through participating distributors and the contractor may pass it on; do-it-yourself installs not eligible.
facts.dates: No end date shown for Washington heat pumps

facts.program: Avista heat pump water heater discount
facts.claim: $500 pass-through discount for a residential retrofit heat pump water heater under 120 gallons (UEF 2.1 or higher); $150 for new construction
facts.eligibility: Contractor discount through participating distributors; Avista electric or natural gas customer; DIY not eligible.

facts.program: Avista Home Insulation Program (Washington)
facts.claim: $1.75 per square foot for attic (R-11 or less to R-49 or more), floor (R-11 or less to R-30 or more) and wall (R-0 to R-11 or more) insulation; $400 per home for duct insulation and $400 for duct sealing; an example of 1,200 square feet of qualifying insulation gets about $2,100; some homes in Named Communities qualify for no-cost upgrades
facts.eligibility: Existing Avista residential customer; primary residence, single-family to fourplex; heats with Avista electricity or natural gas; no income test; approved program installers do a free assessment and take the rebate off the bill. Avista says 10 to 30 percent of homes in its area qualify based on existing insulation.

facts.program: Avista Washington window and sliding glass door rebates
facts.claim: Windows $180 (U-factor 0.29 to 0.23) or $225 (0.22 or below) per window with a contractor, half that for self-install; sliding glass doors $480 or $600 with a contractor, $240 or $300 self-install; storm windows $5.00 per square foot contractor, $4.00 self-install
facts.amount: Up to $225 per window; $600 per door
facts.eligibility: Existing primary single-family homes heated with Avista electricity or natural gas; replacing existing windows; apply within 120 days with the final invoice.

facts.program: Avista Home Weatherization Program (income-qualified)
facts.claim: Free energy-saving upgrades for income-qualifying customers, which may include insulation, air sealing, and door and window insulation
facts.eligibility: Income-qualifying Avista customers; the program page lists income limits
facts.notes: Amounts not read from the program page.
